title: RabbitMQ Messaging
description: Production RabbitMQ reference covering AMQP connections, channels, exchanges, bindings, queues, quorum queues, streams, publishers, confirms, consumers, acknowledgements, retries, dead lettering, flow control, security, clustering, observability, upgrades, and recovery.

subtopics.title: Connections, Channels & Virtual Hosts
subtopics.description: TCP connections are relatively expensive; channels multiplex protocol sessions over a connection. Virtual hosts isolate namespaces and permissions, not physical resources.

codeBlocks.code:
Application process
└─ long-lived connection
   ├─ publisher channel(s) with confirms
   └─ consumer channel(s) with prefetch and acknowledgements

Reconnect connection → reopen channels → redeclare topology → resume

callouts.title: Do Not Share Channels Concurrently Without Client Guarantees
callouts.text: Many clients require per-thread/task channel ownership. Protocol frame interleaving or concurrent confirms can corrupt assumptions even when the connection is shared safely.

subtopics.title: Exchanges, Bindings & Routing Keys
subtopics.description: Publishers send to exchanges; bindings route messages to queues or streams. The exchange type defines how routing keys and binding arguments are matched.

codeBlocks.code:
publish exchange=orders events key=order.paid.eu
topic binding order.*.eu → european-audit queue
topic binding order.# → all-order-events queue

callouts.title: Unroutable Is Not the Same as Unconfirmed
callouts.text: Publisher confirms describe broker handling; mandatory publishing/returns detect messages that matched no queue. Design both outcomes.

subtopics.title: Topology Declaration & Ownership
subtopics.description: Declare durable exchanges, queues, bindings, policies, and arguments consistently. Decide whether applications, operators, or deployment automation owns each resource.

codeBlocks.code:
Application-owned ephemeral reply queue → exclusive + auto-delete
Platform-owned durable business queue → IaC/operator policy
Consumer startup → idempotent compatible declaration
Breaking arguments → migrate to new queue; do not race redeclaration

callouts.title: Inequivalent Redeclaration Closes the Channel
callouts.text: A queue/exchange name with conflicting durable/type/arguments is not silently changed. Version topology migrations and coordinate publishers and consumers.

subtopics.title: Classic Queues, Quorum Queues & Streams
subtopics.description: Choose the data structure from durability, replication, replay, throughput, latency, and consumer semantics rather than treating every workload as a generic queue.

rows: Raft quorum, poison handling, resource cost

callouts.title: Quorum Needs Failure-Domain Placement
callouts.text: A replica count helps only when members span independent nodes/zones and a majority remains reachable. Capacity-plan leader movement and catch-up.

subtopics.title: Publisher Confirms, Persistence & Returns
subtopics.description: Durable topology plus persistent messages and publisher confirms provide broker-acceptance durability; mandatory returns identify unroutable messages.

codeBlocks.code:
1. Publish with stable message ID and persistent delivery mode
2. Track channel sequence number
3. Handle confirm ack/nack asynchronously
4. Handle mandatory return separately
5. On uncertain connection loss, republish safely using idempotency

callouts.title: Confirmation Loss Creates Ambiguity
callouts.text: The broker may have accepted a message even when the publisher missed its confirm. Retried publishing can duplicate; consumers and business effects must be idempotent.

subtopics.title: Consumers, Acknowledgements & Prefetch
subtopics.description: Manual acknowledgements mark completed delivery; nack/reject can requeue or discard/dead-letter. Prefetch bounds unacknowledged work per channel or consumer according to client semantics.

codeBlocks.code:
receive delivery → validate → perform idempotent effect → ack
transient failure → delayed bounded retry path
permanent poison → reject without requeue → quarantine/DLX
shutdown → stop intake → finish or nack owned deliveries → close channel

callouts.title: Immediate Requeue Can Spin
callouts.text: A poison message requeued immediately may consume the same failing worker repeatedly. Use bounded delayed retries and a terminal quarantine with alerts and replay tooling.

subtopics.title: Work Queues, Publish/Subscribe & RPC
subtopics.description: Work queues distribute tasks, fan-out routes events to independent queues, and RPC uses correlation/reply destinations but inherits distributed-call failure modes.

codeBlocks.code:
Work: one durable queue → competing idempotent consumers
Pub/Sub: event exchange → one queue per subscriber responsibility
RPC: request ID + reply-to + deadline + cancellation + duplicate response handling
Prefer asynchronous result/event when caller need not block

callouts.title: Messaging RPC Is Still RPC
callouts.text: It needs deadlines, correlation cleanup, backpressure, authorization, tracing, duplicate handling, and unavailable-service behavior. Do not create unlimited temporary queues.

subtopics.title: TTL, Dead Lettering & Delayed Retries
subtopics.description: Messages can expire by queue or per-message TTL and be dead-lettered on rejection, expiry, length limit, or quorum delivery limit. Policies are easier to operate than hardcoded queue arguments.

codeBlocks.code:
main queue → failure classify
transient → retry exchange → delay queue TTL → dead-letter to main
permanent/exhausted → quarantine queue
operator → inspect reason, repair, replay with same message ID

callouts.title: Dead-Letter Cycles Need Guardrails
callouts.text: Track attempt count and reason, cap retry age/count, avoid routing cycles, alert on quarantine growth, and protect sensitive payload access.

subtopics.title: Flow Control, Memory/Disk Alarms & Backpressure
subtopics.description: RabbitMQ throttles publishers under resource pressure. Applications must bound publish buffers and outstanding confirms rather than accumulating unlimited memory during broker slowdown.

codeBlocks.code:
Bound: connection/channel count, outstanding confirms, client queue, message size
Monitor: memory/disk alarms, blocked connections, publish confirm latency
Respond: slow/reject upstream, shed optional work, preserve critical paths
Never hide prolonged broker pressure with an unbounded local queue

callouts.title: Disk Free Space Is a Safety Threshold
callouts.text: Disk alarms can stop publishers before full exhaustion. Capacity planning must include queue backlog, quorum replicas, stream retention, compaction, paging, and recovery.

subtopics.title: Clusters, Network Partitions & Upgrades
subtopics.description: Cluster metadata is shared, while queue data behavior depends on queue type. Design node identity, peer discovery, failure-domain placement, partition handling, and supported rolling upgrades.

codeBlocks.code:
Before maintenance: quorum health, queue leaders, alarms, capacity, backups
Drain/move leaders where supported → stop one node → upgrade → rejoin/catch up
Verify queues, consumers, confirms, policies and metrics before next node
Never remove multiple quorum members without majority analysis

callouts.title: A Cluster Is Not a WAN Federation Mechanism
callouts.text: Use Federation or Shovel patterns for appropriate cross-site movement and design duplicate, ordering, and outage behavior explicitly.

subtopics.title: TLS, Permissions & Observability
subtopics.description: Use TLS, scoped users or external identity, per-vhost configure/write/read permissions, protected management endpoints, and metrics for broker, queue, connection, and application health.

codeBlocks.code:
Broker: node availability, memory/disk alarms, file descriptors, Erlang processes
Queue: ready/unacked count, publish/deliver/ack rates, consumers, replicas
Client: reconnects, blocked state, confirm latency/nacks, consumer failures
Security: auth failures, permission changes, admin actions, certificate expiry

callouts.title: Do Not Expose Management or AMQP Publicly by Default
callouts.text: Use private networking, strong authentication, least privilege, rate/connection limits, patched clients/brokers, and audited administrative access.

subtopics.title: Definitions, Recovery & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Back up definitions/policies and critical external configuration, but recover message data according to queue type, replica health, site design, and application replay sources.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Choose exchange/queue types intentionally, use confirms and manual acks, make effects idempotent, bound prefetch/retries/buffers, operate DLQs, protect credentials, distribute quorum members, monitor alarms/backlog, test node loss, and rehearse topology and message recovery.
